rulebook: HHSC Minimum Standards for Child-Care Centers (26 TAC Ch. 746), revised December 2025

findings.requirement: Parents may visit the center during hours of operation without prior approval to observe their child and program.
findings.quote: Ensuring parents can visit the child-care center any time during the child-care center's hours of operation to observe their child, program activities, the building, the grounds, and the equipment without having to secure prior approval
findings.handbook_quote: Visit the center any time we are open, without advance notice, to observe your child, activities, the building, the grounds, and equipment

findings.requirement: If the center does not carry required liability insurance, parents must be notified in writing before admission.
findings.quote: If you do not carry liability insurance that meets the requirements of §746.203 of this division (relating to What are the liability insurance requirements?), then you must notify the parent of each child in your care in writing that you do not carry liability insurance before you admit the child into your care.
findings.handbook_quote: We carry liability insurance of $300,000 per occurrence, as Texas requires. If that ever changes, we will tell every family in writing within 14 days.
findings.explanation: The handbook addresses stopping insurance but does not state that parents will be notified in writing before admission if the center does not carry the required insurance.
findings.fix: Insurance: We carry liability insurance of $300,000 per occurrence. If we do not carry this insurance, we will notify you in writing before your child is admitted. If we ever stop carrying it, we will notify every family in writing within 14 days.

findings.requirement: The center must have written operational policies and procedures covering at least the minimum topics listed in the rule.
findings.quote: You must develop written operational policies and procedures that at a minimum address each of the following
findings.handbook_quote: On or before your child's first day, you will sign our enrollment agreement, which includes these policies

findings.requirement: The handbook must state the center's hours, days, and months of operation and its procedures for releasing children.
findings.quote: (1) Hours, days, and months of operation [Medium]; (2) Procedures for the release of children [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: We are open Monday through Friday, 6:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., twelve months a year.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state illness and exclusion criteria and medication procedures or that medication is not dispensed.
findings.quote: (3) Illness and exclusion criteria [Medium]; (4) Procedures for dispensing medication or a statement that medication is not dispensed [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: We are not licensed for get-well care, so children must stay home, or will be sent home, when:

findings.requirement: The handbook must state procedures for handling medical emergencies and for parental notifications.
findings.quote: (5) Procedures for handling medical emergencies [Medium]; (6) Procedures for parental notifications [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: If a child needs immediate medical treatment, we will call 911, give first aid or CPR, call you, contact your child's physician if needed, and keep the other children supervised.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include discipline and guidance consistent with Subchapter L.
findings.quote: Punishment associated with food, naps, or toilet training [High]
findings.handbook_quote: Children who refuse to help clean up may miss that afternoon's snack.
findings.explanation: The handbook uses missing a snack as a consequence, which the rule prohibits.
findings.fix: Children who refuse to help clean up may be redirected or given a brief, age-appropriate time away from the group; we never withhold food, naps, or toilet training as a consequence.

findings.requirement: The handbook must include a safe sleep policy for infants from birth through 12 months old.
findings.quote: Safe sleep policy for infants from birth through 12 months old
findings.explanation: The handbook does not include a safe sleep policy for infants from birth through 12 months old.
findings.fix: Safe sleep for infants: We place every infant on their back to sleep in their own crib. We do not swaddle an infant for sleep or cover an infant's head, face, or crib unless a health-care professional has signed a Sleep Exception Form saying it is medically necessary, and we keep that form in the infant's classroom.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state hearing and vision screening requirements and enrollment procedures, including how and when parents are notified of policy changes.
findings.quote: (12) Hearing and vision screening requirements [Medium]; (13) Enrollment procedures, including how and when parents will be notified of policy changes
findings.handbook_quote: Vision and hearing screening results for children who are 4 years old by September 1, as Texas law requires.

findings.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must state transportation and water activity procedures.
findings.quote: (14) Transportation, if applicable [Medium]; (15) Water activities, if applicable [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: We do not provide transportation, swimming, or water play activities, and we do not keep pets or animals at the center.

findings.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must state field trip and animal procedures.
findings.quote: The notice must be posted at least 48 hours in advance of a field trip.
findings.handbook_quote: We post a notice at the front desk on the morning of each field trip, showing where we are going, when we will leave, and when we expect to return.
findings.explanation: The handbook posts field trip notice on the morning of the trip instead of at least 48 hours in advance.
findings.fix: We post a field trip notice at least 48 hours in advance in a prominent place, showing where we are going, when we will leave, and when we expect to return. The notice stays posted until all children have returned.

findings.requirement: The handbook must promote indoor and outdoor physical activity consistent with Subchapter F.
findings.quote: Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity that is consistent with Subchapter F of this chapter
findings.handbook_quote: We offer at least two outdoor play times every day, weather permitting.

findings.requirement: If applicable, the handbook must state procedures for providing and applying insect repellant and sunscreen.
findings.quote: Procedures for providing and applying, as needed, insect repellant and sunscreen, including what types will be used, if applicable [Medium]
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state procedures for providing and applying insect repellent and sunscreen.
findings.fix: If we apply insect repellent or sunscreen, we will use only the types listed in our policy, follow the product directions, and apply it with your permission; we will tell you which products we use.

findings.requirement: The handbook must state parent rights consistent with Division 5 of Subchapter B.
findings.quote: Parent rights that are consistent with the rules in Division 5 of this subchapter (relating to Parent Rights) [Medium]
findings.handbook_quote: As a parent, you have the right to:

findings.requirement: The handbook must state procedures for parents to review and discuss questions or concerns with the director.
findings.quote: Procedures for parents to review and discuss with the child-care center director any questions or concerns about the policies and procedures of the child-care center [Medium]
findings.explanation: The handbook does not state procedures for parents to review and discuss questions or concerns with the director.
findings.fix: You are always welcome to review and discuss any question or concern about our policies and procedures with the director. Please contact [director name] at [phone/email] to set up a time.

findings.requirement: Children's records must be immediately accessible to caregivers during hours of operation for emergency use.
findings.quote: All children’s records must be immediately accessible to caregivers during hours of operation for use in an emergency.
findings.handbook_quote: Children's records are immediately available to your child's caregivers during all hours of operation in case of emergency.

findings.requirement: Employees must report suspected abuse, neglect, and exploitation to DFPS as required by law.
findings.quote: an employee may not delegate the responsibility to make a report, and you may not require an employee to seek approval to file a report
findings.handbook_quote: Every staff member who suspects abuse, neglect, or exploitation must report it to the director, who will decide whether to call the Texas Abuse and Neglect Hotline.
findings.explanation: The handbook requires staff to report to the director for approval instead of reporting directly to the Texas Abuse and Neglect Hotline.
findings.fix: Every staff member who suspects abuse, neglect, or exploitation must report it directly to the Texas Abuse and Neglect Hotline. We support staff in making reports and do not require approval or notification before a report is made.

findings.requirement: Classroom ratios are based on the specified age of the children in the group and must not be exceeded.
findings.quote: Then the maximum number of children one caregiver may supervise is… 0 – 11 months 4
findings.handbook_quote: Each infant teacher cares for up to six babies, and our infant room holds up to twelve babies when we are full.
findings.explanation: The handbook allows more infants per caregiver and in an infant group than the rule allows.
findings.fix: We follow the Texas child-to-caregiver ratios and group sizes at all times. For infants, that means no more than four babies per caregiver and no more than ten babies in an infant group.

findings.requirement: Infants must be placed face-up for sleep in their own crib unless a health-care professional documents a different position is medically necessary.
findings.quote: You must place an infant in a face-up sleeping position in the infant's own crib, unless you have a completed Sleep Exception Form that includes a signed statement from a health-care professional stating that a different sleeping position for the child is medically necessary

findings.requirement: There must be no harsh, cruel, or unusual treatment of any child, including prohibited discipline practices.
findings.quote: Punishment associated with food, naps, or toilet training [High]
findings.handbook_quote: Children who refuse to help clean up may miss that afternoon's snack.
findings.explanation: The handbook uses missing a snack as a consequence, which the rule prohibits.
findings.fix: Children who refuse to help clean up may be redirected or given a brief, age-appropriate time away from the group; we never withhold food, naps, or toilet training as a consequence.

findings.requirement: Parents must be notified at least 48 hours in advance of a field trip with destination and expected return time.
findings.quote: The notice must be posted at least 48 hours in advance of a field trip.
findings.handbook_quote: We post a notice at the front desk on the morning of each field trip, showing where we are going, when we will leave, and when we expect to return.
findings.explanation: The handbook posts field trip notice on the morning of the trip instead of at least 48 hours in advance.
findings.fix: We post a field trip notice at least 48 hours in advance in a prominent place, showing where we are going, when we will leave, and when we expect to return. The notice stays posted until all children have returned.

findings.requirement: Meals and snacks must follow USDA CACFP meal patterns regardless of reimbursement participation.
findings.quote: The meals and snacks must follow the meal patterns established by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
findings.handbook_quote: We serve breakfast, lunch, and snacks that follow the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program meal patterns.

findings.requirement: Unless licensed for get-well care, an ill child must not attend if the listed illness conditions exist.
findings.quote: Unless you are licensed to provide get-well care, you must not allow an ill child to attend your child-care center if one or more of the following exists:
findings.handbook_quote: We are not licensed for get-well care, so children must stay home, or will be sent home, when:

findings.requirement: Medication may be administered only with parent authorization obtained in writing, electronically, or by telephone for a single dose.
findings.quote: (1) In writing, signed and dated; (2) In an electronic format that is capable of being viewed and saved; or (3) By telephone to administer a single dose of a medication.
findings.handbook_quote: Before we give any medicine, simply tell your child's teacher at drop-off what to give and when; your verbal okay covers the full course of treatment.
findings.explanation: The handbook accepts a verbal okay at drop-off for a full course of treatment instead of written, electronic, or single-dose telephone authorization.
findings.fix: Before we give any medicine, we need your authorization in writing or in an electronic form we can view and save, or by phone for a single dose. A verbal okay at drop-off is not enough, and an authorization expires one year after it is given.

findings.requirement: A food allergy emergency plan is required for each child with a health-care-professional-diagnosed food allergy.
findings.quote: You must have a food allergy emergency plan for each child with a known food allergy that has been diagnosed by a health-care professional.
findings.handbook_quote: If your child has a food allergy diagnosed by a health-care professional, we need a food allergy emergency plan signed and dated by your child's health-care professional and by you before your child's first day.

findings.requirement: A child may be released only to a parent or a person designated by the parent.
findings.quote: You must release a child only to a parent or a person designated by the parent.
findings.handbook_quote: We release children only to a parent or to an adult the parent has listed in writing on the authorized pick-up list.

findings.requirement: The center must practice a fire drill every month and children must be able to exit safely within three minutes.
findings.quote: You must practice a fire drill every month. The children must be able to safely exit the building within three minutes
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a fire drill every month and are able to get all children outside within three minutes.

summary: The handbook covers most required topics but conflicts with the rules on infant ratios, food as a consequence, field-trip notice timing, abuse reporting, and medication authorization. It also omits safe sleep, insect repellent and sunscreen procedures, and parent review procedures, and only partially addresses liability insurance notice.
